overviewSentence: Ky gains a `ky.query()` shortcut for the new HTTP QUERY method, a safe, retryable way to send a request body to a read-only endpoint.
steps: Adding `'query'` to `requestMethods` generates a `ky.query()` shortcut and uppercases the method to `QUERY`.
`KyInstance` and `RequestHttpMethod` learn the new method so it type-checks.
`QUERY` is safe and idempotent, so it joins the default `retry.methods` alongside `GET`.

beforeAfter.caption: How a QUERY request reaches the network

chapters.title: Expose ky.query()
paragraphs: Ky builds its shortcut methods by looping over `requestMethods`, so appending `'query'` there is the whole runtime change: `ky.query(url, options)` now exists and calls `Ky.create` with `{method: 'query'}`. The same list drives `normalizeRequestMethod`, which uppercases it to `QUERY` on the wire.
On the type side, `RequestHttpMethod` gains `'query'` and `KyInstance` declares `query<T>()` with the same signature and docs as its siblings.

chapters.title: Retry QUERY like GET
paragraphs: QUERY is defined as safe and idempotent, so repeating it can't change server state. It is added to the default `retryMethods` list, and the `retry.methods` doc comment shows the new default.
`POST` still isn't retried by default; QUERY gives callers a body-carrying request that is.

chapters.title: Test the new method
paragraphs: New tests check that `ky.query()` sends an uppercase `QUERY` with a JSON body in Node and in the browser, that a lowercase `method: 'query'` is normalized, and that a failing QUERY is retried with the same body each time.

chapters.title: Document ky.query()
paragraphs: The readme lists `ky.query()` with the other shortcuts and adds `QUERY` to the uppercased methods and to the default retry methods.
